– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testTruncateLang59` in the `DateUtilsTest` class is failing because the `DateUtils.truncate` method does not handle daylight saving time (DST) switching hours correctly. The bug report states that when truncating a date at 01:00:00 MDT, the result is actually 01:00:00 MST, which is one hour after the input hour. This discrepancy indicates a problem with how the method treats time zones and DST transitions. Looking at the test code, it sets the time zone to "MST7MDT" and performs truncation operations based on this setup. However, the method fails to account for the transition between standard time (MST) and daylight saving time (MDT), leading to incorrect results. The issue likely lies in how the method handles time zone offsets and DST adjustments during truncation.

To further investigate and confirm this diagnosis, we should analyze the implementation of the `DateUtils.truncate` method in the Apache Commons Lang library.

Next, I will retrieve the code snippet for the `DateUtils.truncate` method to examine its implementation details.
